samples.summary: Flipping YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE to enforce-by-default is a deployment-posture change unrelated to the originating issue, and it ships ahead of the validation its own design doc made a precondition. `docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md`'s rollout section previously staged shadow→enforce as an operational step, and its verb risk explicitly said "the rollout must confirm viewer-link attach/PushPull requests actually carry verb `r` (watch the shadow logs) before flipping". The branch's own lessons file (docs/tasks/active/20260907-notes-share-toolbar-lessons.md:80-85) records that the key part of that question is still open — "whether a *later* presence-only change (a read-only visitor moving their caret) counts toward the Go server's `pack.HasChanges()`; if it does, the design doc's 'a viewer who never edits pushes no changes → verb r' is too strong … the thing to watch first in the shadow-mode rollout window". With the semantics of *unset* inverted, any existing deployment that has already registered the webhook methods and left the variable unset moves from shadow to enforcing on upgrade with no config change, so if that unverified verb path is real, viewer share links lose sync on the deployment rather than in a watched rollout window. The read-gating mitigation (READ_GATED_METHODS) covers attach only, not PushPull. The frontend presence guards added here (pdf-collab, slides-view, board-view) are the acknowledgement that the class of change exists; they bound our own app, not "whether presence makes PushPull rw".
samples.evidence: isYorkieAuthEnforced: `return raw?.trim().toLowerCase() !== 'false'` — unset now enforces, inverting the documented default; lessons doc leaves the presence-verb question unverified while shipping it.

samples.summary: Scope creep relative to the originating issue. docs/tasks/active/20260907-notes-share-toolbar-todo.md scopes issue #1044 to N1–N8 (mount NotesToolbar on the share route, mobile demotion, viewer toolbar, share-token uploader, session-local prefs) plus the engine divider hit area, with an explicit "Out of scope" list. This diff additionally carries: a backend auth-enforcement default flip and new `isYorkieAuthEnforced` helper, a whole new backend service identity (`yorkie-service` token, `decideService`, ops-script token injectors for three scripts), READ_GATED_METHODS, template-review gate rewording, read-only presence guards in pdf/slides/board, `PdfCollabProvider.initialRoot`, and two unrelated jsdom teardown fixes in packages/docs tests (editor disposal / cursor blink interval). Several of those are prerequisites the enforce flip created rather than anything #1044 asked for; bundling them makes the notes change unreviewable and unrevertable independently of the auth change.
samples.evidence: Unrelated docs-package test fix (`const editors: EditorAPI[] = []` + afterEach dispose) shipped in a notes share-toolbar PR; same for the backend service-token subsystem.

samples.summary: `readOnlyNoteStore` is a near-verbatim second copy of `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts` — same reader-allowlist rationale, same memoization map, same nine traps (`get`/`set`/`defineProperty`/`deleteProperty`/`getPrototypeOf`/`setPrototypeOf`/`preventExtensions`/`isExtensible`/`has`/`getOwnPropertyDescriptor`/`ownKeys`), same non-configurable-property exception, same `batch` special case, largely the same comments. Only the allowlist contents and the `HISTORY_METHODS` addition differ. This is a write/access boundary whose value depends on the trap set being complete, and there is now no single place to fix it: the two copies have already diverged (the notes copy corrects the "shadow mode is the default, so this proxy is the write boundary" claim; the docs copy at read-only.ts:40 still asserts it, and lacks the history-method handling). A generic `readOnlyStoreProxy(target, readers, overrides)` in a shared location (the repo's stated convention is shared code in `@wafflebase/core`, cf. docs/design/shared-core-extraction.md) would keep one answer. Note `packages/notes/package.json` does not currently depend on core, so the extraction has a real cost — hence minor, not major.

The change inverts the documented meaning of an unset YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE but only updates two design docs (yorkie-auth-webhook.md, notes/notes.md). The canonical *sharing* doc still states the opposite as load-bearing: sharing.md:208-219 ("This is **off by default**. `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` is unset in a stock deployment, which puts the controller in shadow mode … in the default one the client-side `readOnly` flag is the write boundary") and sharing.md:231-235. That is precisely the claim notes/notes.md now records as wrong. Same stale claim in docs/design/revision-history.md:504-507, docs/design/template-gallery.md:668, docs/design/docs/docs-image-editing.md:300-301, and in code comments at packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:40 and packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4413. Design-doc discipline here means folding the correction into the canonical subsystem docs rather than recording it in one and leaving five contradicting it; nested docs are not covered by the link/ref lane, so nothing will catch this.
samples.evidence: sharing.md:208 "This is **off by default**…" vs docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:29 "Enforcement itself is the **default**".

samples.summary: A comment added by this very diff contradicts the default the same diff establishes: the new read-only rationale in `initialize()` says "the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow (allow-all) mode by default and so may not refuse the write either", while `isYorkieAuthEnforced` added in this change makes enforce the default and notes/notes.md explicitly records that phrasing as the wrong premise ("An earlier draft of this section claimed … That was wrong"). The new premise should be stated once and consistently, or a later feature will again rest on it.
samples.evidence: editor.ts hunk: "…since the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow (allow-all) mode by default and so may not refuse the write either."

samples.summary: The seed command re-implements the public-tier enforcement affirmation (`config.get('YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE') !== 'true'` + its own message) while the change's own comment points at `assertYorkieAuthEnforced`, which is exported from `src/template/template-review.ts` and used by `template.service.ts`. Calling the helper would keep one definition of the affirmation and one message; as written the two can drift (the helper's message was reworded in this diff, the script's was not).

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out against the tree. `isYorkieAuthEnforced` is literally `raw?.trim().toLowerCase() !== 'false'` (yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:29-30), so unset enforces, and it is reachable — the controller reads the env var through it at construction (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:158-161). The claimed narrowness of the mitigation is real: READ_GATED_METHODS contains only 'AttachDocument' (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:108) and is applied only to the verb check (:332-334), leaving PushPull gated on Yorkie's pack-derived verb. The design doc still rests on the unvalidated premise that a non-editing viewer's PushPull carries verb `r` (yorkie-auth-webhook.md:288-292) while conceding shadow mode is the instrument for finding a counterexample (:324), and the branch's own lessons file records that the presence-only PushPull question is still unverified and is "the thing to watch first in the shadow-mode rollout window" (20260907-notes-share-toolbar-lessons.md:80-85). The flip is attributable to this change (lessons :99-104, "enforce is now the default … the one this branch made reachable") and nothing in the originating task scope (20260907-notes-share-toolbar-todo.md:12-38, issue #1044) asks for a deployment-posture change. The cost is concretely demonstrated rather than speculative: the correctness lens confirmed that shared spreadsheet/docs viewers still publish presence unguarded, so a deployment with the methods registered and the variable unset 403s a viewer's sync (.agent-review/correctness/summary.md:5,7). No refutation ground applies — the code is as described, unguarded for PushPull, and unrequested scope creep with a user-visible consequence is in the design-fit lane.
